consent.title: Before you begin
paragraphs: [TEAM: replace with the approved consent text, D1.]

You are invited to take part in a short research study about learning to code. You will answer a short survey, nine multiple-choice coding questions, and a second short survey. It takes about 20-30 minutes.
Taking part is voluntary. You can stop at any time using the 'Stop taking part' link at the bottom of the page, with no penalty.

We do not collect your name, email, student ID or any other identifying information. At the end you will get a random participant code. Keep it if you want to ask for your answers to be removed later.

instructions.title: Instructions
paragraphs: You will now see nine multiple-choice questions about sliding windows, two pointers and arrays.
Questions appear one at a time. Choose one answer and press Submit. You cannot skip a question or go back.
After each answer you will see whether it was correct.
Please work on your own and do not use other websites, notes or tools.
Next there is one more short survey.
Next there is one more short survey.

debrief.title: Thank you for taking part
paragraphs: [TEAM: replace with the approved debrief, D1.]
This study looks at whether game features on coding platforms, such as tokens, badges and leaderboards, change how confident students feel about coding.

Participants were randomly given one of two versions of the same test. Both versions had the same nine questions and told you whether each answer was correct. One version also showed tokens, a badge and a leaderboard. Comparing the two versions lets us see what the game features add.
The leaderboard only ever showed real results from people who took part.
